_units._note: ALL SIZES IN THIS FILE ARE SCREEN PIXELS AT 1x. The builder converts. Height and plan use DIFFERENT constants: world height projects at cos(60)*36.9502 = 18.4752 px per tile, ground depth at sin(60)*36.9502 = 32.0 px per tile. So height_px 6 means 6/18.4752 = 0.3248 world units, and a ground shape is 1:1 with tile width. Stated here so nobody re-derives them, and so nobody uses the wrong one.

_gate: TWO bounds, see art/tools/assert_doodad_contrast.py. (1) median <= ground * median_cap - does it read as an object. (2) p95 <= pooled building p50, MEASURED each run from the shipped sprites - no part of a decoration is as bright as the typical part of a machine. They trade automatically: p95 ~= median * sqrt(internal range), so a busier form gets pushed darker. INTERNAL SHADING RANGE IS UNCONSTRAINED. VALUE ONLY - hue separation is free and unlimited.

_schema.name: output basename; renders to art/sprites/doodads/<name>.png
_schema.kind: 'upright' (blades/leaves standing up) or 'ground' (lies flat on the ground plane)
_schema.height_px: target sprite height in FINAL pixels for upright doodads. Converted to world Z by z = px / 18.4752, because one tile of world HEIGHT projects to WALL_RATIO (0.577) of a tile of screen width, not to a full tile. Asking for '6px tall' in world units would give 11px on screen.
_schema.plan_px: target sprite width in FINAL pixels for ground doodads. Plan is 1:1 - one tile of ground DEPTH projects to exactly 32px, same as one tile of width (see PIPELINE.md 34).
_schema.materials: locked palette member names. Doodads are authored ON palette and so bypass palette_drift entirely - there is no Tripo generation to correct.
_schema.seed: deterministic RNG seed. Same seed must give the same doodad forever, or the sprite changes under people who have approved it.
_schema.albedo_value_scale: scalar on linear albedo, solved by art/tools/calibrate_doodads.py. Uniform across RGB, so palette HUE is preserved exactly and only brightness is given up.
_schema.plan_squash: Y scale on the plan shape. 1.0 = true plan, and it stays 1.0: the camera squashes the ground by GROUND_SQUASH and the anamorphic downsample stretches it back, so ground shapes already arrive at true proportions. Measured on _calib_disc, 1:1 within a pixel. A second squash would make a doodad the only thing disagreeing with its own tile grid. See PIPELINE.md 34.

doodads.name: _calib_disc
doodads.note: A flat unit-diameter disc lying on the ground. Renders through the exact doodad path so the plan aspect ratio can be MEASURED rather than derived. If ground plan shapes arrive at true proportions this comes back 32x32 and round; a stray squash anywhere in the chain shows up here as an ellipse. Never used in game.

doodads.name: _calib_dome
doodads.note: A flat-shaded hemisphere: every normal a ground doodad can present, under the locked rig. Its rendered p95/p5 luminance IS the rig's diffuse dynamic range, and therefore the hard floor under any contrast cap - a doodad cannot be flatter in value than the light falling on it. Committed and measured, never used in game.

doodads.name: grass_tuft
doodads.note: 3-4 upright blades, oak/verdigris mix. Thin and near-vertical, so the key light hits at a grazing angle and it renders dark - which is what lets it clear the contrast cap.

doodads.name: pebble_cluster
doodads.note: Three low stones lying on the ground plane. Faces point UP into the key, which is the hard case for the contrast cap.

doodads.name: weed_clump
doodads.note: Broadleaf, wider than the tuft. Leaves tilt toward horizontal, so it catches more key than the grass does.

doodads.name: fallen_twig
doodads.note: A single stick lying on the ground with one small side branch. Ground plane, so the same key-facing problem as the pebbles.
